message.content:
I’m happy to walk you through how to pull that data yourself, but I don’t have the ability to hit external APIs on your behalf. Below are two practical options:

| Option | API | Key required | Max forecast horizon | Notes |
|--------|-----|--------------|----------------------|-------|
| **Open-Meteo** | https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast | No | 7 days (free tier) | Great for quick, no‑cost requests. |
| **WeatherAPI.com** | https://api.weatherapi.com/v1/forecast.json | Yes (free tier gives 7 days, paid plans give 10 days) | 10 days (paid) | Requires sign‑up for an API key. |

Below are concrete examples for each. Pick the one that best fits your needs.

---

## 1. Using Open‑Meteo (free, no key)

### Request URL

```text
https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=37.8651&longitude=-119.5383&hourly=temperature_2m,windspeed_10m,precipitation_probability,precipitation&forecast_days=7&timezone=America/Los_Angeles
```

> **Explanation of parameters**  
> * `latitude` / `longitude` – your coordinates (note the negative longitude for West).  
> * `hourly=` – comma‑separated list of variables you want.  
> * `forecast_days=7` – maximum free tier horizon.  
> * `timezone=` – local time zone for human‑readable timestamps.

### Sample Response (truncated)

```json
{
  "latitude": 37.8651,
  "longitude": -119.5383,
  "generationtime_ms": 0.234,
  "utc_offset_seconds": -25200,
  "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles",
  "timezone_abbreviation": "PDT",
  "elevation": 1765.0,
  "hourly_units": {
    "time": "iso8601",
    "temperature_2m": "°C",
    "windspeed_10m": "km/h",
    "precipitation_probability": "%",
    "precipitation": "mm"
  },
  "hourly": {
    "time": ["2026-10-01T00:00", "2026-10-01T01:00", ...],
    "temperature_2m": [12.3, 11.8, ...],
    "windspeed_10m": [15.2, 14.9, ...],
    "precipitation_probability": [20, 18, ...],
    "precipitation": [0.0, 0.0, ...]
  }
}
```

> **What you’ll get**  
> * `temperature_2m`: hourly temperature in °C.  
> * `windspeed_10m`: hourly wind speed at 10 m height in km/h.  
> * `precipitation_probability`: chance of precipitation (%).  
> * `precipitation`: actual precipitation amount in mm.

> **Limitations**  
> * Only 7 days of forecast data are available on the free tier.  
> * No historical data or advanced weather models.

---

## 2. Using WeatherAPI.com (requires key, paid plan for 10 days)

### Sign‑up & Get Key

1. Go to https://www.weatherapi.com/ and create a free account.  
2. In the dashboard, locate your **API key**.  
3. Upgrade to the “Pro” plan if you need 10‑day forecasts (the free plan caps at 7 days).

### Request URL

```text
https://api.weatherapi.com/v1/forecast.json?key=YOUR_API_KEY&q=37.8651,-119.5383&days=10&aqi=no&alerts=no
```

> **Parameters**  
> * `key=` – your API key.  
> * `q=` – latitude,longitude pair.  
> * `days=10` – number of days to forecast.  
> * `aqi=no` – omit air quality data.  
> * `alerts=no` – omit weather alerts.

### Sample Response (truncated)

```json
{
  "location": {
    "name": "Yosemite National Park",
    "region": "",
    "country": "United States",
    "lat": 37.8651,
    "lon": -119.5383,
    "tz_id": "America/Los_Angeles",
    "localtime_epoch": 1730000000,
    "localtime": "2026-10-01 00:00"
  },
  "forecast": {
    "forecastday": [
      {
        "date": "2026-10-01",
        "date_epoch": 1730000000,
        "day": { /* summary */ },
        "astro": { /* sunrise/sunset */ },
        "hour": [
          {
            "time_epoch": 1730000000,
            "time": "2026-10-01 00:00",
            "temp_c": 12.3,
            "wind_kph": 15.2,
            "precip_mm": 0.0,
            "precipprob": 20
          },
          /* 23 more hourly entries */
        ]
      },
      /* 9 more forecastday objects */
    ]
  }
}
```

> **What you’ll get**  
> * `hour.temp_c`: hourly temperature in °C.  
> * `hour.wind_kph`: hourly wind speed in km/h.  
> * `hour.precip_mm`: hourly precipitation in mm.  
> * `hour.precipprob`: hourly precipitation probability (%).

> **Benefits**  
> * 10‑day forecast (paid plan).  
> * Rich metadata (sunrise/sunset, UV index, etc.).  
> * Easy to parse in most programming languages.

---

## Quick Python Example (Open‑Meteo)

```python
import requests
import json

url = ("https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?"
       "latitude=37.8651&longitude=-119.5383&hourly="
       "temperature_2m,windspeed_10m,precipitation_probability,precipitation"
       "&forecast_days=7&timezone=America/Los_Angeles")

resp = requests.get(url)
data = resp.json()

# Print first 5 hours
for i in range(5):
    print(f"{data['hourly']['time'][i]} | "
          f"T={data['hourly']['temperature_2m'][i]:.1f}°C | "
          f"W={data['hourly']['windspeed_10m'][i]:.1f} km/h | "
          f"P={data['hourly']['precipitation_probability'][i]}% | "
          f"Precip={data['hourly']['precipitation'][i]:.1f} mm")
```

---

## Quick Python Example (WeatherAPI.com)

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "YOUR_API_KEY"
url = (f"https://api.weatherapi.com/v1/forecast.json?"
       f"key={API_KEY}&q=37.8651,-119.5383&days=10&aqi=no&alerts=no")

resp = requests.get(url)
data = resp.json()

# Print first 5 hours of the first day
first_day = data["forecast"]["forecastday"][0]["hour"]
for hour in first_day[:5]:
    print(f"{hour['time']} | "
          f"T={hour['temp_c']:.1f}°C | "
          f"W={hour['wind_kph']:.1f} km/h | "
          f"P={hour['precipprob']}% | "
          f"Precip={hour['precip_mm']:.1f} mm")
```

---

### Bottom line

* **If you only need 7 days** and want a zero‑cost solution, use Open‑Meteo.  
* **If you need 10 days** (or richer data), sign up for WeatherAPI.com and upgrade to the Pro plan.
